gap: No result ChatGPT got states the 16-inch 2560×1600 screens' figures against Apple's own numbers for the 16-inch MacBook Pro: 188.7 ppi is 74% of the MacBook's 254 ppi, the Duex Float 2 Pro's 65 W pass-through is below Apple's 94 W minimum recommended charging wattage, and a bus-powered UPERFECT GR16EQ drew 5 to 6.5 W (about what the whole MacBook averages in Apple's 17-hour web test) while starting at 30% brightness until its wall brick was plugged in.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best-portable-monitors-for-Mac roundup, PCWorld's roundup and rottenwifi's USB-C/4K/OLED MacBook page, all opened 2026-11-26. Macworld gives 65 W pass-through and 2.9 lb for the Duex Float 2 Pro but no ppi, no power draw for any product and no comparison with the MacBook's charger; its only battery remark is the con 'Laptop battery drain' on the espresso Pro. PCWorld says only that small panels raise pixel density, with no ppi figure and nothing on battery drain. rottenwifi already makes the general weight point ('A nominally 1.5 lb monitor can become a 2.5–3 lb kit') and says a charger needs 'enough wattage for the MacBook after accounting for the display', but gives no watt figure, no ppi, never mentions the 140 W charger and does not cover UPERFECT or SOTSU. So rivals hold the weight-basis idea in general; the ppi ratio, the 94 W line and the bus-power brightness condition are new. RTINGS and TechRadar's roundup were opened but the fetch returned only navigation or the first product, so I could not check their full text. Standout is 2 and not 3 because the bus-power reading was taken on a Steam Deck, not a MacBook, and I could not open the makers' store pages today (HTTP 429).
decides: It confirms 2560×1600 at 16 inches as the line: that is 74% of the MacBook's pixel density, against 56% for the 16-inch 1920×1200 extenders. It puts a condition on ranking the UPERFECT GR16EQ first on brightness: the advertised 450 nits is a figure the one hands-on source only reached with the wall brick plugged in, and on a single cable the screen came up at 30% every time. If that also holds on a MacBook, its lead over the 350-nit Duex Float 2 Pro exists only at a desk with a spare outlet. It also limits the Float 2 Pro's one-cable claim: 65 W pass-through is 69% of Apple's 94 W minimum for this laptop, so it wins the stacked-above-the-screen segment as a screen, not as a charging path. On battery, any of these bus-powered screens roughly halves Apple's web-browsing runtime, so that does not separate them.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro / M5 Max) display, the reference every row is normalised to
findings.value: 16.2-inch, 3456 × 2234, 254 ppi, ProMotion up to 120 Hz, SDR up to 1000 nits outdoors
findings.note: Apple's figures. Half of native in each direction (Retina 2×) is 1728 × 1117 points.

findings.label: Pixel density of a 16-inch 2560×1600 panel against the MacBook's own
findings.note: Arithmetic: √(2560² + 1600²) = 3018.9 px ÷ 16 in = 188.7 ppi; 188.7 ÷ 254 = 0.743. Applies to GR16EQ, GR16DQ, FlipAction Pro 16, Duex Float 2 Pro and Fold 16 QHD alike, so it sets the line and does not rank within it. To show the same 1728-point-wide workspace as the MacBook, a 2560-wide panel has 1.48 pixels per point against the MacBook's 2.0.

findings.label: Pixel density of the 16-inch 1920×1200 panels left below the line
findings.note: Arithmetic: √(1920² + 1200²) = 2264.2 px ÷ 16 in = 141.5 ppi; ÷ 254 = 0.557. This is the FOPO S11 / S9G / S788 class. For scale, a 15.6-inch 3840×2160 panel is 282.4 ppi (111%).

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro battery and its own average draw in Apple's tests
findings.value: 99.6 Wh; about 5.9 W in the 17-hour wireless-web test and 4.2 W in the 24-hour video-streaming test (M5 Pro)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 99.6 ÷ 17 = 5.86 W; 99.6 ÷ 24 = 4.15 W. M5 Max is 16 h web (6.2 W) and 22 h video (4.5 W). Apple markets the battery as 100 Wh; the footnote gives 99.6 Wh.

findings.label: Power drawn from the host over one USB-C cable
findings.source_title: uperfect gr16eq monitor (Steam Flow review, posted on UPERFECT's blog 2026-06-30)
findings.note: Steam Flow: 'The monitor draws between 5 and 6.5 watts from the Steam deck when it's running off just the USB-C cable.' Host was a Steam Deck, not a MacBook. UPERFECT supplied the unit and hosts the review. Normalised: 5.86 W + 5 to 6.5 W = 10.9 to 12.4 W, so 99.6 Wh lasts about 8.1 to 9.2 h against Apple's 17 h web figure, roughly half.

findings.label: Brightness on one cable against the advertised 450 nits
findings.value: Defaults to 30% brightness on bus power; full brightness needs the wall brick
findings.source_title: uperfect gr16eq monitor (Steam Flow review, posted on UPERFECT's blog 2026-06-30)
findings.note: Steam Flow: 'the monitor will default to 30% brightness every single time' and 'You need the charging brick plugged in to get the full brightness and save your settings.' The reviewer calls 450 nits the advertised figure and says 'I can't scientifically test this', so no nits were measured. The included brick is 20 W; with it the monitor takes 5 to 6 W. Steam Deck host: behaviour on a MacBook port is not established by this source.

findings.label: Refresh rate by cable, against the MacBook's 120 Hz
findings.value: 144 Hz over USB-C; mini HDMI tops out at 130 Hz at 2560×1600
findings.source_title: uperfect gr16eq monitor (Steam Flow review, posted on UPERFECT's blog 2026-06-30)
findings.note: Steam Flow: 'if you want the full 144 Hz, use USB-C' and 'The Mini HDMI caps out at 130 Hz at this resolution.' The MacBook's own panel tops out at 120 Hz (Apple), so the 24 Hz above that is not a match advantage. Apple lists external displays at up to 4K/144 Hz for M5 Pro.

findings.label: Weight as a reviewer describes it
findings.source_title: uperfect gr16eq monitor (Steam Flow review, posted on UPERFECT's blog 2026-06-30)
findings.note: Steam Flow: 'the whole thing weighs under 1 kg'. Not a scale reading. The desk note says the store states 0.75 kg in the copy and 1.04 kg net in the spec table; this quote fits the first and conflicts with the second. I could not re-read the store page today.

findings.label: Pass-through charging against what Apple says the 16-inch MacBook Pro needs
findings.value: 65 W pass-through; 69% of Apple's 94 W minimum recommended charging wattage, 46% of the 140 W adapter in the box
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026: Top lightweight displays for your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: 65 W is Macworld's listed figure for the Float 2 Pro. 94 W minimum and 140 W adapter (needed for fast charging) are from https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/ read 2026-11-26. Arithmetic: 65 ÷ 94 = 0.69; 65 ÷ 140 = 0.46. Whether the 65 W is before or after the screen's own draw is not stated.

findings.label: Weight against the MacBook it stacks above
findings.value: 2.9 lb (1.3 kg); 62% of the MacBook's 4.7 lb, 7.6 lb for the pair
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026: Top lightweight displays for your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld's figure; it does not say whether the stand and magnets are included. MacBook Pro 16 weight 4.7 lb (2.14 kg M5 Pro, 2.15 kg M5 Max) from Apple's spec page, read 2026-11-26. Arithmetic: 2.9 ÷ 4.7 = 0.62.

findings.label: Panel as Macworld lists it
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026: Top lightweight displays for your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: 'Up to' figures, not labelled as measured. 350 nits is 35% of the MacBook's 1000-nit outdoor SDR ceiling; I did not get Apple's indoor SDR figure. 120 Hz equals the MacBook's ProMotion ceiling. Macworld does not say which cable it used or which refresh rate macOS reported.
